title: RED Metrics
subtitle: Request-scoped microservice health telemetry: Rate, Errors, and Duration for standardized service dashboards.
keyTakeaways: The RED method (Rate, Errors, Duration) measures the external user experience of request-driven microservices, contrasting with the resource-oriented USE method (Utilization, Saturation, Errors).
Standardizing RED metrics across every RPC/HTTP boundary lets teams auto-generate identical service dashboards and topology health maps without custom per-team queries.
Always partition Duration histograms by error status so fast-failing 500s do not artificially lower perceived p50/p99 latency.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: Popularized by Tom Wilkie (Weaveworks/Grafana), the RED method provides a uniform black-box contract for every stateless or stateful request-handling service. When every service emits the exact same metric schema via middleware or service-mesh sidecars (Envoy), on-call engineers can diagnose unfamiliar services immediately.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: The RED method (Rate, Errors, Duration) measures the external user experience of request-driven microservices, contrasting with the resource-oriented USE method (Utilization, Saturation, Errors).

**Problem Space & Invariants**: Standardizing RED metrics across every RPC/HTTP boundary lets teams auto-generate identical service dashboards and topology health maps without custom per-team queries.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for RED Metrics:
bullets: **Service-Mesh Sidecar RED Telemetry (Envoy / Istio)**: Provides 100% uniform red metrics across polyglot services with zero application code changes. Best suited for Platform engineering teams governing dozens of microservices in different languages.

**In-App Middleware Instrumentation (OpenTelemetry SDK)**: Provides access to exact framework route patterns (e.g., `/users/:id`), internal business errors, and custom attributes. Best suited for Core services needing fine-grained endpoint attribution and semantic error classification.
Rate: The number of requests per second the service is handling (`sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))`).
Errors: The number of failed requests per second (`status=~'5.'` or gRPC codes `Unavailable`, `DeadlineExceeded`), expressed as a ratio of total Rate.

Fast-Fail Latency Distortion: When a database circuit breaker trips, requests fail in 1ms with HTTP 503. If 5xx responses are mixed into the latency histogram, overall p99 latency appears to improve during an outage!
Client vs Server RED Perspective: Emit RED metrics on both the server middleware and the outbound RPC client stub to immediately isolate network/load-balancer delays from application execution time.

codeSnippet.title: Standardized RED Recording Rules in Prometheus
codeSnippet.code:
groups:
  - name: service_red_metrics
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      # 1. Rate (Requests per second per service)
      - record: service:http_requests:rate5m
        expr: sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total[5m]))

      # 2. Error Ratio (5xx responses / total responses)
      - record: service:http_errors:ratio5m
        expr: |
          sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5."}[5m]))
          /
          sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total[5m]))

      # 3. Duration (p99 Latency in seconds for successful requests)
      - record: service:http_request_duration_seconds:p99_5m
        expr: |
          histogram_quantile(0.99,
            sum by (service, le) (rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{status!~"5."}[5m]))
          )

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply RED Metrics across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for Platform engineering teams governing dozens of microservices in different languages, suited for environments requiring 100% uniform RED metrics across polyglot services with zero application code changes.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for Core services needing fine-grained endpoint attribution and semantic error classification, where Access to exact framework route patterns (e.g., `/users/:id`), internal business errors, and custom attributes.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: While RED measures customer-facing work, Brendan Gregg's USE method (Utilization, Saturation, Errors) measures underlying hardware and OS resources (CPU, disks, network NICs, thread pools). Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of RED Metrics introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: lacks application-level route templates unless configured; adds proxy cpu/memory overhead.
**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: requires sdk version upgrades and enforcement across all application repositories.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for RED Metrics:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: Always partition Duration histograms by error status so fast-failing 500s do not artificially lower perceived p50/p99 latency.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Point out the 'fast-fail paradox' in interviews: always compute Duration quantiles separately for successful (`2xx`) and failed (`5xx`) requests so a circuit-breaker outage returning instant 503s doesn't mask latency degradation.
